answer: Each identity binds to one iris code. An orb scans the applicant once, signs a hash, and the registry harbors only that hash, never a raw image. A duplicate hash is rejected instantly, so one human holds exactly one identity. Each epoch the agent presents a fresh live scan; a mismatch against the stored hash freezes all claims. No one can forge a matching code without the living eye, so 100 clones need 100 distinct people, each spending about 5 and one hour on an orb visit: $2,500 and 100 hours total. Every reward thread runs back to that single scan, like a ship tied to one berth.
